$comment: Which XML containers may have their child elements sorted, and by what key.
Deliberately small. These three are the only containers known to be
order-insensitive in practice. Everything else is left exactly as exported,
including anything that merely looks sortable.
The XPaths are ABSOLUTE, rooted at the document element. That is the main
safety property: /Entity/EntityInfo/entity/attributes cannot accidentally
match an 'attributes' element somewhere else in a different document, the
way a '//attributes' wildcard would. A rule only fires on a document whose
root element matches.
container : absolute XPath selecting the parent whose children get sorted.
child     : element name to sort. Other children are left in place.
keys      : ordered XPaths relative to each child, tried in order.
Attributes ('@Name') and nested paths ('Required/@schemaName')
both work. A child matching no key sorts by its own XML, which
is arbitrary but stable, so the result stays deterministic.
Adding a rule is a real decision, not a configuration tweak. Confirm
against a real export that the container exists with the expected keys,
then confirm with a round trip that the solution still imports. Form
layout, ribbon definitions and sitemap ordering are positional: sorting
them changes behaviour or breaks import.
